touches.text: HYPOTHESIS marks a mechanism written as a first draft so that experiments have something to be wrong about. It is not a decision; what the experiments show replaces it (Law 3).
Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work.
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal. Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#90 (a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal, measured 2026-11-12): "then we have to invent a way for seals to be host independent. one way would be to create a sealing machine in cairn. there's only ever one cairn until we have a laptop die and have to fail over to a backup".

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Akien 2026-11-13: "every test failure, every orphaned file, HAS TO BE FIXED. if we get 3 reds but they're really not related to what we just did, we can ticket them for fixing. reds don't get lost." and "so each run writes any new bugs". Once a red unrelated to a crossing is ticketed, that crossing can go ahead.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, "because even the basic laws rest finally upon those core principles" (Akien 2026-11-13). Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).

[Q#101: proofgate reads the text of a Bash command, so a proof run from a script file ("bash run_it.sh", whose text names no proof) is invisible to it. Measured 2026-11-13: such a proof runs bare and writes into the live HOME/.cairn. Which should seal that spelling? (a) every proof refuses to run unless it is inside the tester's seal, as one check in a shared helper or at the scratch door; (b) the hook also reads the script file a bash/sh command names; (c) a proof run from a script file is accepted as outside the rule. CC leans (a): it is the only one that covers every spelling, not just the next one found. This reopens ticket 72a37498c601's WRONG INTENT clause; ticket dda0e72b9c67 clause 4 waits on it (open-49fc67a40ede).]

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.

The one writer question is LLM or code (Akien 2026-10-28: "there is no point in tracking the 'authoring entity' ... Whether the write came from an LLM or from deterministic code is really the only question", and only for gate-pass certificates). So on Windows the caller class comes from the process chain: claude.exe above the writer means cc; otherwise it is not cc. Env vars are a fallback only. Certificates are made where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), so Windows does not need a gate class of its own. CC's decision, 2026-11-13, on Q#91 (3 teeth of test_artifact_door.py UNRAN on Windows, measured 2026-11-12).

conflicts.text: HYPOTHESIS marks a mechanism written as a first draft so that experiments have something to be wrong about. It is not a decision; what the experiments show replaces it (Law 3).
conflicts.ticket_says: chart.orient.unknowns: 'the posix run was not made: the changes are guarded by _has_linux_callers() and os.name == 'nt', so posix behaviour is unchanged by construction only'
conflicts.why: Falsifier clause 3 claims 'on a posix box the proof's results are unchanged' but the validate section measures only Windows and explicitly admits posix behavior was not measured. HYPOTHESIS (0.7) describes first drafts for experiments; what the experiments show replaces it (Law 3). An unmeasured claim in the falsifier contradicts Law 3 ('Nothing is known until measured') and 9.4.2.3's requirement that proofs measure against their falsifier. The ticket cannot have both a falsifier clause 3 and a validation that omits it.

conflicts.ticket_says: falsifier has three clauses (clauses 1, 2, 3) but validate section covers only one criterion matching clause 1 and implicitly clause 2, leaving clause 3 (posix unchanged) unvalidated
conflicts.why: The tester's INTENTION (9.4.2.3) requires proof runs to measure their falsifier. If a falsifier clause exists and is not measured, it violates the proof structure. Either clause 3 must be removed from the falsifier or measured in validate; the mismatch cannot stand.
